items.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening of-phrase
secondary_features: subject-verb agreement across an intervening prepositional phrase
items.sentence: The retreat of the continental ice sheets that once covered northern Europe have left behind thick deposits of gravel and clay.
items.error_explanation: The head of the subject noun phrase is the singular noun 'retreat'; the of-phrase 'of the continental ice sheets' and the relative clause 'that once covered northern Europe' only modify it and cannot supply the subject. A singular head requires the singular auxiliary 'has', so the plural 'have' is an agreement failure produced by attraction to the nearer plural noun. The relative clause already contains its own finite verb 'covered', so 'have left' cannot be construed inside it. 'that' correctly introduces a restrictive relative clause whose antecedent is 'ice sheets', 'thick' is an adjective correctly modifying 'deposits', and 'gravel' is a mass noun correctly used after 'deposits of'.

items.subtype: possessive determiner number agreement with its antecedent
secondary_features: possessive determiner agreement with a plural antecedent
items.sentence: During the coldest months, humpback whales migrate toward the tropics in order to raise its calves in warm coastal water.
items.error_explanation: The understood subject of the purpose infinitive 'to raise ... calves' is the matrix subject 'humpback whales', which is plural, so the possessive determiner must be the plural 'their'. The singular 'its' has no number-compatible antecedent anywhere in the sentence, since every other nominal ('the coldest months', 'the tropics', 'calves') is plural; the defect is therefore a formal number-agreement failure rather than a matter of preferred interpretation. 'coldest months' is a correctly formed superlative after 'the', 'migrate' correctly agrees with the plural subject 'whales', and 'the tropics' is a correctly used plural-only noun.

items.subtype: redundant determiner after a quantifier phrase
items.sentence: Even after the British Parliament imposed duties on imported goods, the most of the colonial merchants continued to trade abroad.
items.error_explanation: In the partitive quantifier phrase 'most of the colonial merchants', the quantifier 'most' takes no preceding article, so the definite article in 'the most of' is an extraneous determiner and must be deleted. Standard written English licenses 'the most' only as a superlative marker before an adjective or adverb, not as the head of a partitive of-phrase functioning as a clause subject. 'after' correctly subordinates the finite clause that follows, 'imposed duties' is a correctly formed past-tense verb plus object, and 'merchants' is a correctly formed plural count noun.
